A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CleanDIFT and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The original material can be matched across renumbering and relocation, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original semantic correspondence, depth estimation, segmentation, and classification experiments, together with ablations and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds experiments on text conditioning, training datasets, supervised correspondence, and additional diffusion backbones.

M1.justification: The core feature-alignment procedure, projection heads, and cosine objective remain unchanged. Appendix B adds a variant that distills text conditioning to enable prompt-free inference; Appendix F adapts larger backbones using LoRA instead of full fine-tuning.

E1.justification: The four downstream task families and their evaluation datasets are retained. v2 adds a prompt-free correspondence scenario and uses SPair71k and ImageNet as alternative fine-tuning sources; these datasets previously appeared in evaluation rather than CleanDIFT fine-tuning.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1, 2, 4, and 5 are retained. Appendix B adds the supervised TLFR aggregation comparison, reporting 83.2 for standard SD2.1 features versus 83.9 for CleanDIFT, beyond the retained supervised Diffusion Hyperfeatures comparison.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends evaluation settings through supervised TLFR with per-image PCK, prompt-free controls, alternative fine-tuning datasets, and SDXL, SDXL Turbo, PIXART-alpha, and Flux experiments with timestep/feature-map sweeps. Larger models use rank-64 LoRA. Table 3 also drops 'subset' from its caption while Section 4.6 retains it, leaving the revised ablation evaluation population unresolved.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained loss, projection-head, and timestep analyses, v2 tests caption distillation against training without captions, sensitivity to fine-tuning data, and applicability across backbone architectures. Figure 16 adds a feature PCA analysis. These address several previously untested questions about conditioning, data dependence, and generality.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The retained eight-noise-sample DIFT averaging is an inference procedure, not newly added uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2, 4, and 5 retain their values, but Table 3 replaces the ablation scores and reverses the L1-versus-L2 ranking; cosine with heads changes from 67.61/60.28 to 68.32/61.43, with split comparability unresolved. New results include supervised TLFR's 83.9 versus 83.2, prompt-distillation gains of 1.2 over prompt-free DIFT and 0.4 over unconditioned CleanDIFT, dataset scores of 61.42/61.43/60.78, and four-backbone gains in Table 7.

T1.justification: The diffusion definitions, cosine-alignment loss in Equation 1, and stratified timestep-sampling rule are retained. Neither version provides additional theorems or proofs, and the new appendix experiments introduce no substantive formal derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the claims of noise-free, timestep-independent features, inexpensive adaptation, improved downstream performance, and reduced inference cost. The added experiments support these existing claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly states that standard CleanDIFT needs a suitable prompt for optimal performance. It adds interpretations that target-test-data fine-tuning provides no advantage over COYO, mismatched ImageNet training reduces performance, and gains persist across backbone sizes and architectures. The central explanation of noise harming diffusion features is retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents zero-initialized residual projection heads, their 45M parameters, image-caption training, the correspondence prompt, approximately 3k COYO images, and LoRA targets and rank. These improve implementation disclosure, although Appendix G's minimum image size of 768 squared conflicts with the retained 512 squared description in Section 4.1.

R1.justification: v2 adds eight references, including a diffusion-representation survey, SODA, DreamTeacher, diffusion-feature distillation, LoRA, and additional backbone works. Related-work coverage expands modestly while the existing positioning around general-purpose diffusion features and distillation remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 polishes several passages and rewrites the conclusion while retaining its meaning. It merges the Fused Features paragraph into the surrounding discussion and separates the former Projection Heads appendix into depth-probe analysis and projection-head ablations. The main narrative and section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The overview and most quantitative plots are redrawn with revised axes, legends, line styles, and annotations. Qualitative figures are relocated, the main correspondence panel is shortened, tables are reformatted, and Tables 6–7 and Figure 16 are added. Figure 10 introduces an inconsistent SD2.1 legend while Section 4.5 still specifies SD1.5.

improvement.justification: The new conditioning, backbone, and training-data studies better support CleanDIFT's applicability, while additional implementation details help reproducibility. These benefits are limited by reporting inconsistencies: revised Table 3 implies projection-head gains of 0.16/0.14 rather than the retained prose's 0.24/0.06, and the ablation split, COYO filtering, and Figure 10 backbone labeling are unclear. The net gain is useful but limited.
